title: Quarter-hour frequency steps
question: Is the grid frequency further from 50 Hz in the first two minutes after each quarter-hour than in the rest of the quarter-hour, compared per quarter-hour of the day?

issues.text: Seconds are strongly autocorrelated, so a test over 86,000 seconds would overstate the evidence.
issues.fix: The plan averages each quarter-hour's two windows and tests the 96 paired differences.

issues.text: The data shows when deviations happen, not that market schedules cause them.
issues.fix: The caveats name the mechanism and what would test it: generation schedules and load (Energy-Charts public_power) at the same 15-minute steps.

alternatives.question: Is the step larger at the full hour than at :15, :30 and :45?
alternatives.why: Drill down: hourly products are still traded alongside quarter-hours.

alternatives.question: Does the size of the step follow the change in scheduled generation between quarter-hours?
alternatives.why: Expand: brings in the schedules that are said to cause it.

hypotheses.statement: The mean |Δf| in the first two minutes of a quarter-hour is larger than in the rest of it.
hypotheses.null: |Δf| is the same in the first two minutes as in the rest of the quarter-hour.

hypotheses.statement: The frequency changes faster (larger |df/dt|) in the first two minutes of a quarter-hour.
hypotheses.null: |df/dt| is the same in both windows.

concepts.label: Frequency deviation
concepts.description: Grid frequency minus 50 Hz, in mHz, per second.
concepts.why: The outcome: the grid's power balance.

concepts.label: Quarter-hour window
concepts.description: First 2 minutes of a quarter-hour or the rest of it.
concepts.why: The predictor: where schedule steps fall.

concepts.label: Generation schedule
concepts.why: The proposed cause of the steps.

strategy.detail: Energy-Charts /public_power?country=de (15-minute generation and load), matched on the quarter-hour.

data.request: Germany's 15-minute net generation and load for the same day
data.why: To see whether the frequency step follows the change in generation at each boundary.

method.summary: For each of the day's 96 quarter-hours, mean |Δf| in its first two minutes minus the rest; a one-sided t-test on the mean difference (the quarters step computes it).

steps.title: Label each second
steps.detail: window = first 2 min if t mod 900 < 120, else rest.

steps.title: Average per quarter-hour and window, then pair
steps.detail: quarters and paired steps: mean_abs_df_mhz per quarter and window, one row per quarter.

steps.title: Paired t-test
steps.detail: test step: t_abs_df, p_abs_df_one_sided, ci95_lo…ci95_hi; and the same for |df/dt|.

steps.title: Accept or reject H1 and H2
steps.detail: Then repeat on other days (change start and end) before generalising.

caveats: One day at one measuring point; the pattern changes with season, weekday and the hour of day.
Quarter-hours next to each other are not fully independent (slow drifts last longer than 15 minutes).
A first-2-minute window is a choice; the fold chart shows where the step really is.
Association, not cause: the market-schedule mechanism is the operators' explanation, not tested here.
